entries.title: CASE FILE
entries.body:

Vitals: weight 79 kg, height 175 cm, BMI 25.8, BP 123/64 mmHg, HR 80 bpm. Smoking: Ex-smoker (33 pack-yr, quit 2021).

Chief complaint: Request for clinical re-evaluation driven by previous biopsy results and a current PSA elevation to 5.3 ng/mL.

History: A 56-year-old retired bank clerk first entered investigation during early 2023 after a PSA elevation triggered a positive biopsy and subsequent monitoring protocol. He is married and shares his residence with his partner, maintaining a fairly active routine that includes cycling roughly 20 kilometres twice weekly. Lower urinary tract symptoms register at a moderate IPSS of 11, with no reports of pelvic pain or haematuria. After accumulating 33 pack-years of smoking, he ceased tobacco use in 2021. Alcohol intake stays near one unit per week. Unrelated urological issues include uncomplicated cataract surgery performed three years prior and routine podiatry visits. He previously opted out of research trials and currently maintains a BMI exceeding 30 without any active medications.

Physical examination: DRE — texture: moderately enlarged gland with a distinct Nodus palpable in the left peripheral zone; mobility: unrestricted. General assessment shows stable vital signs, absent lymphadenopathy, and no bone tenderness.

Patient info: retired bank clerk; Married; Lives with partner.
Next of kin: Spouse / partner (primary contact).

Lifestyle: alcohol 1 units / week; exercise Cycling 2x/week, ~20 km; IPSS score: 11/35 (moderate LUTS).

Recent other appointments: Podiatry — routine foot care.
Admin: Patient declined research participation previously; respect for AS-related trials.

Question:

entries.speaker: EXPERT-PRIOR
entries.role: statistical expert; k-NN over 8 structured variables of THIS prompt only, trained on 91 labelled cases, leave-one-out honest
entries.title: INITIAL RECOMMENDATION (statistical prior)
entries.body:
A basic classifier, whose sole purpose is to provide a suggestion, produces this result along with its associated uncertainty. The purpose of this decision is to use it as an initial reference point for discussing the results.

SUGGESTION: NO BIOPSY
  p(biopsy = yes) = 0.27 +/- 0.18   (95% CI 0.02-0.69)

Where the uncertainty comes from:
  - aleatoric  dA = 0.15  (the nearest labelled cases disagree with each other)
  - epistemic  dA = 0.10  (few labelled cases resemble this one)
  - 5.2 effective neighbours out of 10; 0 of the 5 closest labelled cases were biopsied
  - 80%-coverage conformal set: {no}

TIER 'supports': A +/- dA does not cross 0.5, but A +/- 1.96*dA does. There is a direction, not a conclusion. Measured accuracy in this tier: 0.67. Treat it as a weighted vote, not as a decision.

Variables it actually read (from the visible panel only, no documents retrieved):
  pirads=4.0, bx_ord=3.0, psa=5.3, age=56.0, psad=0.1, dre_ord=1.0, vol=48.0, n_pmhx=1.0
  missing / not evaluable: none

Out-of-fold performance of this recommender on the 91 labelled cases (5x5 CV):
  accuracy 0.703, balanced accuracy 0.662, AUC 0.75, ECE 0.095.
It is right about 7 times out of 10 overall. It is NOT an oracle and it has never seen the
radiology report, the PSA trajectory, the laboratory panel or the previous notes.

data.lectura: A ± ΔA no cruza 0.5: hay una dirección clara pero no cerrada. Sirve como voto con peso, no como decisión.
data.nota_entrenamiento: El caso está entre los 91 etiquetados; se ha excluido de sus propios vecinos, así que esta respuesta es honesta.

entries.speaker: EXPERT-PROTOCOL
entries.role: protocol expert; applies the guideline criterion for this patient's clinical situation
entries.title: GUIDELINE CRITERION FOR THIS SITUATION
entries.body:
CLINICAL SITUATION: prior positive biopsy.

THIS CRITERION RETURNS NO ANSWER FOR THIS PATIENT.

The criterion: The visible panel does NOT determine this decision. The patient already has a tissue diagnosis, so neither a high PI-RADS nor a rising PSA is new information. The decision must come from the retrieved documents: whether the prior grade is documented, whether the lesion changed against a previous MRI, whether a surveillance re-biopsy is due, and whether treatment is already agreed.

Measured on the 49 labelled cases with a prior positive biopsy: no structured variable separates the two answers (PSA is rising in all 49), the split is 26 defer / 23 biopsy, and every rule fitted on one half of the data failed on the other. This is genuinely undetermined by the panel.

Do not read this as 'defer' and do not read it as 'biopsy'. It means the panel cannot settle the case and the retrieved documents must.

Like the statistical prior, this expert has read ONLY the visible panel. It has not seen the
mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the laboratory panel.

entries.speaker: LLM-1-GAP-ANALYST
entries.role: raises doubt only; has no access to clinical documents and issues no recommendation
entries.title: GAPS AND DOUBTS
entries.body:
WHAT THE PRIOR CANNOT SEE
The statistical recommender only used the visible panel data (PI-RADS=4.0, PSA=5.3, PSA density=0.1, DRE=Nodus, Volume=48.0 mL, Prior Biopsy=Positive, csPCa probability=0.4028) and could not account for the context provided by the retrieved documents, such as the specific MRI findings, PSA velocity, or the history of prior biopsy outcome.

WHY THE SUGGESTION COULD BE WRONG
The prior suggested 'NO BIOPSY' with a wide uncertainty interval (0.27 +/- 0.18). This wide interval suggests the model is highly uncertain, which could be misleading. Specifically, the prior failed to weigh the combination of a PI-RADS 4 score with a rising PSA velocity (2.26 ng/mL/yr) against the prior positive biopsy result, which the protocol expert noted is undetermined by the visible panel alone. The prior might be wrong because it did not incorporate the specific risk stratification matrix derived from the guidelines, which could lead to an incorrect assessment of the risk profile.

WHAT TO RETRIEVE, AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER
radiology / mpMRI report - does the lesion compare with a previous MRI? - if it is unchanged the case for sampling weakens; if new or larger it strengthens
PSA history - trend / velocity beyond the headline value
previous GP / urology notes
laboratory panel
The retrieval of the mpMRI report is critical because the guideline mentions that MRI-directed biopsy is the standard of care, and the report will clarify if the PI-RADS 4 lesion has changed, which directly impacts the decision pathway.

GUIDELINE ANCHOR
The guideline search indicates that the decision depends on whether the prior grade is documented, whether the lesion changed against a previous MRI, and whether a surveillance re-biopsy is due.

entries.title: FINAL DECISION AND FORM
entries.body:
FINAL DECISION: BIOPSY   (confidence: borderline)

Although the prior positive biopsy suggests deferral, the rising PSA velocity of 2.26 ng/mL/yr and the presence of a PI-RADS 4 lesion warrant re-evaluation per the guideline criterion. The evidence retrieved shows the PSA trend rising from 3.5 ng/mL to 5.3 ng/mL, which, combined with the PI-RADS 4 finding, suggests the need to re-characterize the lesion. The conference resolved the conflict by leaning toward sampling because the retrieved data indicated a change in clinical status despite the prior diagnosis.
